answer: Cohort bonds stop Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer joins nine random established agents and posts a $20 share of a $200 bond. Second, two members countersign each job, staking their share, so trust grows like a pearl. Third, one fraud burns the pool and freezes the newcomer 90 days, so guards audit hard. Fourth, after thirty clean days it graduates and guards the next cohort, its record, a sonnet. Faking 1,000 agents costs $20,000 in bonds plus 9,000 bribes at $50, over $470,000 lost. Like roommates sharing one deposit, one broken window costs all ten; trust moves like a glacier.
